items.text: A local ceasefire in and around Russian-occupied Oleshky took effect at 03:00 Kyiv time (04:00 Moscow). Ombudsman [[p:Dmytro Lubinets]] says both sides are keeping to it, and Russia's defence ministry says its forces have stopped firing on the Kherson front. Lubinets says the aid and evacuation mission itself is due to start on 29 Oct, after mine clearance. Minutes after the truce began, Russia hit Kyiv with ballistic missiles and drones, killing one person and injuring at least 14.
items.notes: Kyrylo Budanov, now head of the President's Office, also announced the start. Kyiv Independent (Rebecka Pieder), citing AP, says the freeze should last until at least Saturday 31 Oct. Kyiv strike: the Air Force says Russia launched 280 drones (69 jet-powered) plus ballistic missiles from Bryansk oblast; 255 drones and 2 missiles were downed, with hits at 25 sites. A Desnianskyi university dormitory and metro infrastructure on the Pivdennyi Bridge were damaged (Hromadske, Artem Hetsko: https://hromadske.ua/en/war/273236-russian-attack-on-kyiv-kills-one-injures-14-damages-metro-bridge). The injured count varies: 14 in the headline and most sources, 21 in Hromadske's meta description.

items.text: [[p:Flávio Bolsonaro]] dropped his plan to seek annulment of the runoff after his [[p:Liberal Party|Liberal Party (Brazil, 2006)]] (PL) recognised Lula's win. Instead, his team will pursue cases seeking the removal of Lula's ticket for alleged abuse of political and economic power. On the same day, [[p:Donald Trump]] told reporters the election looked rigged, criticising a court-ordered extension of voting hours, though he said he gets on well with Lula.
items.notes: PL president Valdemar Costa Neto said questions about the vote still need answering; the party blames pre-election social spending. Retreat: ND Mais (Lidia Gabriella), citing CNN and unnamed campaign sources, says 20 cassação requests have already been filed (https://ndmais.com.br/politica/flavio-bolsonaro-desiste-de-pedir-anulacao-da-eleicao-e-muda-estrategia-para-tentar-cassar-chapa-de-lula/). Background: STF Justice Cristiano Zanin extended voting by two hours at Lula's coalition's request. TSE president Nunes Marques said the extension did not change the result but could have compromised the whole election (Metrópoles, 25 Oct). The Trump quote comes from Gazeta do Povo (John Lucas); Reuters/US News headline: 'Trump says Brazil election looked rigged'. No Brazilian government response was found.

items.text: A drone strike on a market in Nyala, the [[p:Rapid Support Forces]]' de facto capital, killed at least 21 people and wounded about 40, according to a hospital medic cited by AFP. The RSF says the toll is 102 dead and 113 wounded and blames an army drone; the army has not commented. Earlier the same day, RSF drones knocked out power stations in Gezira, Sennar, Gedaref and White Nile states.
items.notes: Toll conflict: AFP/medical source says 21 killed and 40 wounded; RSF spokesman Col. Al-Tayeb Khalil says 102 and 113 (Radio Tamazuj, Tryag News: https://tryagnews.com/85999). Neither the toll nor the perpetrator is independently verified. The strike was at about 20:00 local time on 26 Oct in Doumayya/Tanqoung market. Power-station strikes: Al-Jineid (Gezira), Sinja (Sennar), Al-Fao and Al-Hawata (Gedaref) and Mashkour (White Nile), per Sudan Tribune (O Mohamed) and Al Jazeera Arabic. Arab League chief Nabil Fahmy arrived in Khartoum on 26 Oct. The link2 cross-check covers the power strikes only; MC Doualiya (Arabic) also carries the AFP Nyala toll.

items.text: Both chambers of Algeria's parliament unanimously approved sending army units to Niger to protect energy infrastructure in the north of the country. It is Algeria's first military deployment abroad since the 1973 Arab–Israeli war. Troop numbers and timing have not been announced. The move follows a visit to Algiers by Niger's defence minister and a new military cooperation protocol.
items.notes: This happened on 25 Oct, just before the window, but it is not in already_logged and is Tier 1 for the Sahel. The Council of the Nation (upper house) voted on 25 Oct; the People's National Assembly vote was reported the same evening (Reuters/US News; newscord.org: unanimous). Algeria sent Su-30 jets to Niamey in August. Algerian officials describe the mission as protecting economic infrastructure, not waging war. Al Jazeera analysis on 26 Oct: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/26/algerias-military-deployment-to-niger-whats-behind-the-move

items.text: With all ballot samples counted, CeSID projections give the Student List 53% and 141 of 250 seats, against 39% and 103 seats for [[p:Aleksandar Vučić]]'s [[p:Serbian Progressive Party]]. Vučić blamed his defeat on European governments and the 'US deep state', and predicted the new government would impose sanctions on Russia; Student List figures say it will not. The Kremlin said it hopes Belgrade will keep cooperating with Russia, and [[p:Friedrich Merz]] pledged to support Serbia's EU path.
items.notes: The movement has no single leader. Possible names include Ilija Srdanović (list head), Dejan Šoškić (ex-central bank governor) and Radomir Saičić. Parliament must convene within 30 days of official results, and a government must be formed within 90 days after that. A presidential election must be held before 27 Dec because Vučić resigned. Student List figure Aleksandar Baucal said 'sanctions against Russia will not be imposed' (Meduza). Zelensky called the result a 'new chapter'.

items.text: The [[p:Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party]] opened its four-day fifth plenum, where [[p:Xi Jinping]] presented a work report and a draft decision on 'full and rigorous party self-governance'. Reuters reports that analysts see it as possibly the last major gathering before the 2027 leadership reshuffle, at which Xi is expected to seek a fourth term. A communiqué is due when the plenum closes on 29 Oct.
items.notes: No outcomes yet; watch the 29 Oct communiqué for Central Military Commission and Central Committee personnel changes after the military purges. Six provinces announced personnel changes, including two new party chiefs, on 24 Oct (Reuters). Unusually, this plenum focuses on party discipline rather than economic policy. The Wikipedia article for the plenum could not be verified, so it is left unlinked.

items.text: Romanian prosecutors (DIICOT) and the [[p:Romanian Intelligence Service]] say a Russian network coordinated the 14 Sept arson near CARFIL, a subsidiary of state arms maker [[p:Romarm|ROMARM]] in Brașov. The three alleged perpetrators, two Belarusians and a Ukrainian, were reportedly coerced by Russian operatives. Two were arrested while allegedly preparing similar attacks in Germany, and a European arrest warrant was issued for the third, believed to be in Poland.
items.notes: This is an attribution in an official joint DIICOT/SRI release; the SRI called it part of a wider Russian sabotage campaign in Europe. No Russian response was found. The Romanian-language original was not retrieved, so a second source is needed. Possibly Tier 2.

items.text: After their Tehran talks with [[p:Mohsen Rezaei]] and President [[p:Masoud Pezeshkian]], the three [[e:Mecca defence pact|Mecca Joint Defence Agreement]] states and Iran said only that they would continue their dialogue on regional security. They set no ceasefire terms and no date for another meeting. A Pakistani official told Reuters that [[p:Asim Munir]] presented a compromise proposal, with Trump's backing for diplomacy, under which the pact states and Qatar could act as guarantors. The terms were not disclosed.
items.notes: The joint-statement wording comes from Al Jazeera/Reuters and Geo/AFP (https://www.geo.tv/latest/688392-cdf-munir-in-tehran-as-iran-hosts-makkah-pact-nations-amid-escalating-houthi-attacks). According to NIAC, the agenda also covered a regional non-aggression network, Hormuz, the US blockade and the Houthis. Iranian SNSC deputy Ali Baqeri-Kani says Munir proposed the meeting. Zarif's 'West Asian Security Network' idea was left out of the communiqué. Saudi deputy minister Rayed Krimly called the visit de-escalation in support of the Qatari and Pakistani mediation. Iran is demanding a return to the June memorandum and an end to the blockade, and the US has rejected the memorandum (Motamedi).

items.text: [[p:Masoud Pezeshkian]] flew to Moscow for the eighth [[p:Gas Exporting Countries Forum]] summit and met Qatar's Emir [[p:Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani]] on the sidelines. Kremlin aide [[p:Yuri Ushakov]] says [[p:Vladimir Putin]] will hold five bilateral meetings at the summit, including with Pezeshkian and the emir. Pezeshkian said US actions are disrupting global energy flows.
items.notes: IRIB describes it as a one-day visit. The Putin–Pezeshkian meeting had not been read out when we checked. Putin's other bilaterals are with Mozambique's Chapo, Equatorial Guinea's Obiang and Libya's al-Menfi (TASS). Iran International's liveblog (09:07 GMT) reports the meeting with the Qatari emir. The talks follow up Lavrov's visit to Tehran on 19 Oct. Hamshahri reported the Putin meeting as confirmed (https://www.hamshahrionline.ir/news/1080456), but we could not open the page.

items.text: Egypt's [[p:House of Representatives|House of Representatives (Egypt)]] approved President [[p:Abdel Fattah el-Sisi]]'s request to send forces on a defensive mission to Saudi Arabia against [[p:Houthi|Houthis]] attacks. The mandate does not set troop numbers. Sisi says the mission covers Saudi territory only and will not include attacks on Yemen. A Houthi media official urged Cairo to mediate instead, while Houthi allies called the decision a declaration of war.
items.notes: Article 152 of the constitution requires a two-thirds majority. BBC Arabic, via Cedar News, says the vote was taken standing and passed by a near-absolute majority, with the Egyptian Democratic Party bloc (about 12 MPs) abstaining. Sisi's statement says support would extend to any Arab state that asks. The Houthi official who urged mediation is Nasr al-Din Amer. CBS cites Houthi allies for the 'declaration of war' description. The vote had been delayed on 19–20 Oct.

items.text: Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki says strikes in Houthi-held Yemen destroyed five ballistic-missile storage tunnels, four launchers and a missile depot. The [[p:Houthis]] claim a missile hit Riyadh's King Khalid airport and have told airlines to avoid Saudi airspace. On 27 Oct the coalition said it intercepted three ballistic missiles aimed at the Eastern Province and four drones.
items.notes: Neither side's claims have been independently verified. BBC Arabic (via Cedar News) reports Houthi claims of 56 coalition strikes on Yemeni towns, and that the Al Nassr–Al Wasl Asian Champions League match in Riyadh was postponed because flights were cancelled. Houthis also claimed drone hits on oil pumping stations. Saudi Arabia lifted its threat alerts in the central and eastern regions early on 27 Oct (Reuters via JPost).

items.text: Asharq Al-Awsat reports that government forces repelled Houthi assaults around besieged Taiz and on the Kahbub front near Bab al-Mandab, with the Giants Brigades and Homeland Shield taking part. Government forces say they struck a Houthi command centre and two tanks in Taiz's disused Sofitel hotel.
items.notes: The outlet is Saudi-owned. It reports unverified claims that unnamed Houthi leaders were killed and that an ambush in Hayjat al-Abd (Lahj) killed or wounded dozens. It reports no government casualties.

items.text: The US State Department ordered non-emergency staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, citing escalating [[p:Houthi|Houthis]] attacks on airports and infrastructure. On the same day, an attack on Dammam's King Fahd airport killed one person and injured eight, and a drone strike on [[p:Saudi Aramco]]'s Shaybah oilfield killed two.
items.reporter: Rami Ayyub, Humeyra Pamuk, Timour Azhari
items.notes: State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott says the order covers Saudi Arabia only. Four US officials said other Gulf missions would withdraw families. This is separate from the cuts in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and the UAE logged under E-261025-15. Saudi Arabia postponed the FII conference to 2027 on 19 Oct, outside the window.

items.text: Kuwait's criminal court (state security circuit) sentenced three men to death, one of them an Iranian national, for spying for Iran and [[p:Hezbollah]] and plotting to assassinate First Deputy PM and Interior Minister [[p:Fahad Yusuf Al-Sabah]] and other officials. Eight co-defendants received five years. The verdict can be appealed.
items.notes: Asharq Al-Awsat names the condemned as Hussein Abdullah Al-Matouq, Hassan Abdulhadi Hajieh and Abdulreza Haidar Dehqani (Iranian). The presiding judge was Nasser Al-Badr. AFP via CBS says the condemned are Shia and that 11 others got five years of hard labour; Kuwait Times and Asharq Al-Awsat say eight.

items.text: Satellite images show an oil slick spreading along the UAE's northern coast. Umm Al Quwain and Ras Al Khaimah closed all their beaches, and Sharjah closed Al Hamriyah beach. Authorities have not named the source, but experts told Reuters it is the tanker Gem No.2, hit by an unidentified projectile last month.
items.notes: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment said on 23 Oct that it is containing a leak from an offshore tanker. Al Jazeera reported the slick reaching UAE shores on 25 Oct. Reuters' original is at usnews.com/news/world/articles/2026-10-26/oil-spill-off-uae-widens... (we could not fetch it).

items.text: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority, the body Tehran set up to license Hormuz transits and which the US has sanctioned, says it will take legal action from 1 Nov against vessels of South Korea's Sinokor over alleged passage violations. Iran International reports that enforcement action has already been taken against at least seven of the company's ships.
items.notes: The warning comes alongside IRGC claims of mine and missile hits on 'unauthorised' vessels (E-261025-08). Seatrade reported earlier strikes on Sinokor ships. Iran International's English edition is London-based and hostile to the government.

items.text: [[p:UKMTO|United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations]] reported a vessel on fire about 63 nautical miles southeast of Iraq's al-Faw and called it 'suspicious activity'. On 20 Oct UKMTO had reported a tanker hit by an unidentified projectile about 30 nm southeast of al-Faw, with no damage and the crew safe. An Iraqi source told Shafaq News that Iraqi authorities had not confirmed that strike.
items.notes: No cause or casualties have been reported for the 26 Oct fire. The 20 Oct incident is UKMTO warning 180-26.

items.text: As the government prepares for a winter gas shortfall, parliament speaker [[p:Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf]] called for gas use to be cut by at least 10%. Executive vice-president Mohammad-Jafar Ghaempanah has told officials that attacks on refineries leave a shortfall of about 100 million cubic metres a day, and that per-province consumption quotas will be set with the president.
items.notes: The Shana article is undated (it refers to 'this week' and 'next week') and we confirmed it was online by 27 Oct. Shana is the Oil Ministry's news agency.

items.text: US Treasury Secretary [[p:Scott Bessent]] told Iranians to stock up on petrol and heating fuel and predicted their economy would shrink by more than a quarter in the year to March 2027. Kpler told the WSJ that Iran's oil held on shadow-fleet tankers ran out in mid-October. [[p:CENTCOM|United States Central Command]] says the [[e:naval blockade|2026 United States naval blockade of Iran]] has cost Iran at least $25bn in crude exports.
items.notes: CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper also claims the IRGC cannot pay its soldiers. Central Bank governor Abdolnaser Hemmati calls talk of collapse 'an illusion' (Motamedi, Al Jazeera, 20 Oct). The World Bank projects a 7.7% contraction in 2026-27, far less than Bessent's figure. The rial was about 2.64 million per dollar in Tehran around 23 Oct (Al Jazeera).

items.text: Foreign ministry spokesman [[p:Esmail Baghaei]] said Tehran has not closed the diplomatic window and that messages to Washington are still passing through intermediaries. He added that the result of Israel's election makes no difference to Iran. On 27 Oct Iranian officials said the US is not serious about talks, and FM [[p:Abbas Araghchi]] said a renewed war would not change Iran's positions.
items.notes: On 25 Oct Trump told Fox he must decide whether to 'finish it off' or make a deal (CBS). That remark overlaps with E-261025-09. NIAC and earlier reporting say the White House has ruled out strikes before the 3 Nov midterms. Also on 27 Oct, government spokeswoman Fatemeh Mohajerani said Iran wants peace but will respond to any attack, and Araghchi phoned his Egyptian and Jordanian counterparts (Iran International).

items.text: Parliament speaker [[p:Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf]] said Supreme Leader [[p:Mojtaba Khamenei]] is in full health and that the two had discussed economic indicators and protecting purchasing power. Khamenei has not appeared in public for months amid rumours about his health.
items.notes: The claim is attributed to Ghalibaf and comes with no independent footage. The background on Khamenei's absence comes from earlier reporting by IranWire, Ara and others.

items.text: MP Abolfazl Aboutorabi urged Iran to leave the [[e:NPT|Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons]] and build a nuclear bomb. He said a withdrawal would have to be coordinated with the Supreme National Security Council and claimed the Pickaxe Mountain tunnels could withstand a nuclear strike.
items.notes: This comes as the UN Security Council holds an Iran non-proliferation briefing with Grossi on 27 Oct (see watch). An NPT-exit bill has been pending since March. SNSC chief Rezaei said on 21 Oct that 'not a single gram' of enriched uranium will leave Iran (E-261025-56).

items.text: Kurdish rights group Hengaw reports that Iran executed five prisoners on 18 and 21 Oct in Semnan, Qezelhesar (Karaj) and Shiraz's Adelabad prison: three on drug charges and two for murder. It says state media and the judiciary did not report the executions.
items.notes: Earlier political cases (Ali-Sina Mostafavi, 14 Oct; Omar Dorostaran; an Iraqi man executed for alleged spying for Saudi Arabia) fall before the window. Iran Human Rights counts 17 espionage executions in 2026.

items.text: [[p:IranWire]] reports that security forces seized the phone of Ali Haji, a teachers' union activist in Jolfa, and interrogated him over social-media posts about those killed in the January 2026 protests. The teachers' trade associations' coordinating council condemned the pressure.
items.notes: The phone was seized on 11 Oct and he was interrogated on 17 Oct. It has not been returned despite a prosecutor's order.

items.text: Brent crude settled around $116 a barrel on 26 Oct and was little changed early on 27 Oct, near its highest since April. IMF PortWatch counted only four Hormuz transits on 18 Oct, against a pre-war norm of about 85 a day. Tanker owners' group INTERTANKO says more than 30 ships a day use the US-backed route.
items.notes: straits.live gives Brent at $115.99 at 18:12 UTC on 26 Oct and WTI at $102.05. PortWatch and INTERTANKO count transits differently. WTI is about $14 below Brent.

items.text: Four figures arrested in the 'Dawn Crackdown' anti-corruption sweep face trial between 26 Oct and 8 Nov. They include MP Ziad al-Janabi, Azm Alliance leader Muthanna al-Samarrai and Mohammed al-Sayhoud of ex-PM Sudani's coalition. Authorities say cash and gold were seized from properties linked to them.
items.notes: The source is unnamed. The trial dates are al-Janabi 26 Oct, oil-products distribution director-general Hussein Talib 27 Oct, al-Samarrai 29 Oct (postponed on 19 Oct) and al-Sayhoud 8 Nov.

items.text: Shafaq News reports that [[p:Kataib Hezbollah]] rejects PM [[p:Ali al-Zaidi]]'s timetable to bring faction weapons under state control by 30 June 2027, while [[p:Asaib Ahl al-Haq]], whose leader Laith al-Khazali became a deputy PM on 15 Oct, has announced integration steps. Nujaba and others say they will disarm only if foreign forces leave.
items.notes: A 90-day de-escalation period started on 1 Oct and ends around the turn of the year, which Shafaq sees as the key date. Parliament completed al-Zaidi's cabinet on 15 Oct. The IMF projects Iraq's economy will shrink 16% in 2026. Opinion: analysis

items.text: King [[p:Charles III]] hosted Sultan [[p:Haitham bin Tariq]] for a state visit at Windsor Castle. The palace's account mentions no agreements.
items.notes: Oman is party to a temporary Hormuz transit arrangement with Iran, which Tehran wants the US to recognise (Al Jazeera, 21 Oct). No new Omani mediation was reported this week.

items.text: Israelis are voting in the [[e:2026 Israeli legislative election]]. About 7.33 million people are eligible to vote at 12,018 polling stations. The Central Elections Committee put turnout at 16.68% (about 1.2 million voters) at 10:00, up 0.78 points on 2022 and the highest for that hour since 1981. Polls close at 22:00, when exit polls are due. The last weekend polls gave neither bloc 61 seats.
items.notes: ToI headline says 'since at least 1996' but its 11:07 entry says 'since 1981'; N12 also says 1981. Final four-poll average (Maariv, 25 Oct): Yashar 22, Likud 19.75, Bennett's B'Yachad 14.5, opposition 54 vs Netanyahu bloc 49.5, Arab parties 14.5; Ofer Winter's People of Israel below 3.25% threshold (https://www.jpost.com/israel-election-2026/article-912743). No later hourly turnout was published by the time of writing. ToI results livestream from 21:30.

items.text: Police arrested three men from Negev Bedouin communities overnight on suspicion of paying people to vote for [[p:Ra'am|United Arab List]], seizing envelopes holding tens of thousands of shekels. Eisenkot's Yashar filed an urgent complaint about missing or stolen ballot slips. Finance Minister [[p:Bezalel Smotrich]] claimed without evidence that high turnout was driven by Arab and left-wing voters. The election committee said there were fewer irregularities than in 2022.
items.notes: Other complaints: Yisrael Beytenu (Likud slip pre-placed in envelope in Beersheba), People of Israel (slips missing); Bennett's party accused Likud of tracking voters, which the CEC disputed. ToI sidebar: Likud reportedly preparing to claim the vote was 'stolen' if it loses; not independently confirmed. A Yashar billboard was torched in Dimona overnight.

items.text: Israel Hayom reports that the Trump administration is pushing for a post-election unity government of [[p:Benjamin Netanyahu]] and [[p:Gadi Eisenkot]] that would leave out [[p:Itamar Ben-Gvir]]. It cites unnamed US sources. Under the reported plan, Netanyahu would serve about two years, end the wars and sign regional deals, then retire. The office of President [[p:Isaac Herzog]] denied any involvement in pardon talks. Eisenkot's camp would reportedly demand Netanyahu's retirement and a state inquiry into 7 October.
items.notes: On 27 Oct Ben-Gvir attacked the reported plan and urged voters to strengthen him (ToI liveblog 11:27). Eisenkot has repeatedly ruled out serving under Netanyahu, though the report says he has recently softened his wording. US ambassador Huckabee says Washington will work with any elected government. Maariv carried a similar report on a post-election 'Iran card' to force unity (https://www.maariv.co.il/news/military/article-1380570).

items.text: Channel 13 aired footage of Education Minister [[p:Yoav Kisch]], with Netanyahu on the phone, agreeing to give a deputy-minister post to the small Haredi party Achi if it left the race. Achi's spiritual leader, Rabbi Haim Yosef Abergel, faces charges of sexual offences against minors. Likud had confirmed the deal when Achi withdrew. [[p:Naftali Bennett]] called it a corrupt deal.
items.notes: Kisch said Likud would try to change the law so that a non-MK could serve as deputy minister. Also on 25 Oct Netanyahu posted an AI image of a nuclear strike on Tel Aviv, warning of a '2nd Holocaust' if he loses; Eisenkot called him 'hysterical'. The Sydney Morning Herald reports that James Packer paid $1.25m to Netanyahu's defence firm (Case 1000).

items.text: Netanyahu told a business TV channel that Israel must prepare an economy that can get around possible international sanctions, including by using cryptocurrency. The [[p:Bank of Israel]] said on 24 Oct that crypto cannot be used to evade sanctions and that Israel should work to prevent them. More than 100 senior economists, including Nobel laureate [[p:Joel Mokyr]], warned that sanctions would destroy Israel's economic model.
items.notes: Netanyahu later told Channel 14 that crypto is 'one of the means' and that he is not sure it will be used. Nahum Barnea (Ynet, 26 Oct) notes Netanyahu has said European and US sanctions are coming, and that the Netherlands has taken symbolic measures against settlement goods.

items.text: The October Council, a group of 7 October survivors, freed hostages and bereaved families, held a rally in Tel Aviv's [[p:Hostages Square]] demanding a state commission of inquiry. Organisers say more than 100,000 attended; police gave no estimate. Opposition leaders including Eisenkot, Bennett, [[p:Yair Lapid]], [[p:Avigdor Liberman]] and [[p:Yair Golan]] attended. The election committee chair rejected Likud's request to block the broadcast.
items.notes: Netanyahu refuses a state commission, arguing that a Supreme Court-appointed panel would be biased. Some outlets say 'thousands' rather than 100,000. JPost: 7 Oct families planned rallies outside polling stations on election day.

items.text: Kan reports that army chief [[p:Eyal Zamir]] told Netanyahu at a 25 Oct meeting that the Hebron operation had met its goals. He said there was no legal basis to keep displaced Palestinians from returning home. Netanyahu ordered the operation to continue; Haaretz reports that Defence Minister [[p:Israel Katz]] also blocked the army's plan to end it. WAFA puts the number displaced since 23 Oct at about 3,971, and the Palestinian Prisoners' Club reports more than 80 arrests.
items.outlet: Srugim (citing Kan News); The New Arab
items.notes: A military source says troops searched about 500 buildings and found one rifle and one pistol. Displacement figures differ: Katz said about 2,000 (E-261025-11), the PA 2,670 on 25 Oct, WAFA 3,971 on 26 Oct. The Hebron governor counts 128 gates and 120 checkpoints. The IDF imposed a general closure on West Bank Palestinians for election day (Haaretz, 25 Oct). Haaretz link: https://www.haaretz.com/west-bank/2026-10-26/ty-article/.premium/netanyahu-katz-blocked-idf-plan-to-end-hebron-raids-allow-locals-to-return/000001a1-777e-dfb9-a5a9-ff7f15ce0000 (not fetchable).

items.text: Gaza civil defence says Israeli fire killed 11–13 people in the 24 hours to 26 Oct. They include three people, one a seven-year-old girl, killed in a strike on a displacement camp in al-Mawasi, west of Khan Younis. Residents say Israeli tanks advanced west of the Yellow Line in eastern Deir al-Balah. The IDF said it was looking into the Mawasi strike, and said separately that it targeted nine 'terror operatives'.
items.thread: Gaza ceasefire and Board of Peace plan
items.notes: The health ministry says more than 1,500 people have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire and 74,555 since the war began. The New Arab adds two killed in a vehicle strike in Deir al-Balah. ToI reports a strike on the Islamic University building and Hebrew-media reports of a Hamas threat over the advances. Israel is estimated to control over 60% of the Strip.

items.text: In a report to the UN General Assembly, the UN Commission of Inquiry on the occupied Palestinian territory says Israel is continuing to commit genocidal acts in Gaza despite the ceasefire. It says Israeli control of the Strip has grown from 53% to at least 60%. It accuses Israel of crimes against humanity in the West Bank, where it counts more than 34,000 displaced. Israel rejected the report as a misinformation campaign and called for the commission to be dissolved.
items.notes: The commission counts at least 196 Palestinians killed by Israeli fire along the advancing line since the ceasefire, 43 of them children; the Gaza health ministry says more than 1,400. It also records 254 West Bank deaths from Israeli airstrikes from October 2023 to September 2026.

items.text: Albania signed its participation agreement with the [[p:International Stabilization Force]] for Gaza, offering operations support and planning, with liaison officers due in November. Kosovo says its bomb-disposal team is ready but awaiting a green light. No ISF unit has deployed yet: the [[p:Board of Peace]] is still seeking Israeli approval, including for a base near the Yellow Line.
items.thread: Gaza ceasefire and Board of Peace plan
items.notes: ISF commander US Maj. Gen. Jasper Jeffers attended the signing. Contributors so far: Morocco (up to 500 trained), Kazakhstan, Kosovo and Albania. Israel's security cabinet approved entry of about 200 troops in July. A Board official hopes for progress after the election; the plan is stalled over Hamas disarmament and the order of Israeli withdrawals.

items.text: Reuters, citing Lebanese security sources and a person close to [[p:Hezbollah]], reports that the group has spent about three months preparing for renewed war with Israel. It has focused on explosives and attack drones, using what the sources say are tens of millions of dollars in fresh military funds from Iran. Israel's military declined to comment, and the US says it will keep sanctioning Hezbollah's finances.
items.thread: Lebanon: Hezbollah disarmament and Israeli occupation
items.notes: Both links carry the same Reuters story; no independent confirmation. The new funds come on top of about $200m Iran sent earlier for displaced families. Hezbollah denies that its command structures broke down. Israeli troops still occupy southern villages and keep up strikes. Asharq Al-Awsat reports that war-weary Shi'ite supporters are pressing the group to stay out of a new war.

items.text: A Lebanese judge summoned two Hezbollah officials for questioning over a shipment of about half a tonne of explosives seized on 8 Oct at a checkpoint in Dahr al-Baidar. Hezbollah MP Hassan Fadlallah has said the explosives belong to the group and are meant for use against Israel. Security services are trying to locate the two officials.
items.thread: Lebanon: Hezbollah disarmament and Israeli occupation
items.notes: Authorities have seized three large explosives shipments this month. Rubio has urged Beirut not to return them. President Aoun and PM Salam pledge action against weapons outside state control under the June Lebanon–Israel framework. On 18 Oct Netanyahu said he does not trust Beirut to disarm Hezbollah and that troops will stay in the south (Asharq Al-Awsat).

items.text: Jordan's armed forces carried out airstrikes on what they called terrorist hideouts in Syria's Daraa and Suwayda provinces in response to the [[e:Karak church attack|2026 Karak church shooting]]. Amman said the strikes were coordinated with Damascus; Syria denied any coordination, said seven civilians including three children were killed, and closed the [[p:Nassib crossing|Nasib Border Crossing]]. Jordan also arrested three suspects, two brothers and their brother-in-law, after a three-hour shootout in Karak governorate.
items.notes: Jordan named the operation 'Jordanian Deterrence – Hamud'. Death tolls differ: Syrian Civil Defence 7, Enab Baladi lead 5, Asharq Al-Awsat 8, WaPo 5. A Syrian foreign ministry official called it a 'treacherous attack'. The armed group targeted was not named. The Karak toll stands at at least nine dead. Wikipedia article: '2026 Jordanian strikes on Syria'.

items.text: Israeli forces shot dead Muath Salameh al-Bairi, a young man with a disability, during an incursion into Jamla in western Daraa countryside. Syria's foreign ministry condemned the killing. The Sijil Center recorded 280 Israeli violations in southern Syria in September, and no Syria–Israel security agreement has been reached.
items.notes: The IDF has not commented. Verify-Sy debunked a video shared as showing the Jamla attack; it was filmed in the West Bank. Enab Baladi analysis (25 Oct) says analysts see little difference between Netanyahu and Eisenkot on Syria policy.

items.text: Families of Suwayda detainees held by the Syrian government, some for over a year, blocked the Damascus–Suwayda road to demand their release and a new prisoner exchange. The government's Suwayda media office blamed a checkpoint of the local National Guard for the closure and said hundreds of supply trucks were stranded.
items.notes: The families say the detainees are held at Adra prison. A US-mediated exchange on 26 Feb freed 61 Suwayda detainees in return for 30 Defence and Interior Ministry personnel.

items.text: The Supreme State Security Prosecution questioned [[p:Lina Attalah]], editor-in-chief of [[p:Mada Masr]], on 21 Oct and released her on bail of 100,000 Egyptian pounds. The next day it referred her for trial on a charge of running an unlicensed website, with a first hearing on 27 Oct. A conviction could bring a fine of up to EGP 3m and closure of the outlet; it is the sixth case against Mada Masr in six years.
items.outlet: Human Rights Watch; The New Arab
items.notes: The summons followed a Mada Masr report on abuse complaints by prisoners. Six journalists from the fact-checking platform Matsada2sh have been held since 28–29 Sept on terrorism and false-news charges. CPJ counts 25 journalists jailed in Egypt. Outcome of the 27 Oct hearing not yet known. Amnesty and more than 100 groups have urged an end to the case.

items.text: A bill to ratify the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, signed with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan on 7 Aug, was submitted to the [[p:Turkish parliament|Grand National Assembly of Turkey]]. Under the pact, an attack on one country counts as an attack on all three. An AKP MP told Reuters that a motion to send Turkish military personnel to Saudi Arabia will follow ratification, starting with air-defence and electronic-warfare experts who would not take part in offensive operations.
items.notes: The bill goes first to the Foreign Affairs Committee; no date is set. The opposition warns that it could drag Turkey into the Yemen war, and AKP and MHP votes defeated a CHP motion for a general debate. On 21 Oct Turkey, Qatar, Pakistan and Indonesia signed a 'Badr' defence-cooperation memorandum in Doha.

items.text: The [[p:Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey]] cut its one-week repo rate from 37% to 36%, its first cut since January. It said underlying inflation is easing but high energy prices tied to geopolitical tensions are an upside risk. It promised to keep policy tight and to decide meeting by meeting.
items.notes: Overnight lending rate cut to 39% and borrowing rate to 34.5%. September annual inflation was 29.73%. Most economists expect another cut in December. Goldman Sachs warned that reserves fell $30bn in 12 months.

items.text: A court jailed Ertan Aydın, a former chief adviser to [[p:Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] and ex-AKP MP, pending trial in the market-manipulation probe linked to the investment-fund crisis. Prosecutors had appealed his earlier house arrest. Aydın sat on the board of Tera Yatırım, the brokerage at the centre of the crisis, in 2025. Total arrests in the probe reached 114 on 24 Oct.
items.thread: Turkey fund crisis and opposition crackdown
items.notes: About half a million investors could not withdraw savings in September. The Capital Markets Board (SPK) ordered 131 funds liquidated, and its chairman Mahmut Sütcü resigned on 19 Oct. Parliament passed a repayment law on 22 Oct allowing interim payouts of up to 1m lira. Those arrested include Altınbaş Holding's İnan Altınbaş and former central bank deputy governor Taha Çakmak. Aydın denies signing any documents.

items.text: The Interior Ministry suspended Milas mayor Fevzi Topuz of the [[p:CHP|Republican People's Party (Turkey)]], three days after a court jailed him and his son pending trial on bribery, forgery and organised-crime charges. The case concerns allegedly fake tender documents; 18 of 35 people detained in raids across 13 provinces were jailed. Separately, Çukurova's mayor and 33 others were jailed in Adana.
items.thread: Turkey fund crisis and opposition crackdown
items.notes: On 20 Oct suspended Bolu mayor Tanju Özcan (CHP) was sentenced to over seven years for extortion. Also on 20 Oct an Istanbul court ordered Özgür Özel, now leader of the New Party (Yeni Parti), to pay Justice Minister Akın Gürlek 750,000 lira in damages, and on 21 Oct the Constitutional Court rejected a bid to force the New Party to change its name (institude bulletin). Cumhuriyet (Sept) says Kılıçdaroğlu was installed as CHP chair by court ruling.

items.text: At the second hearing of the 'official car' abuse-of-office case against jailed Istanbul mayor [[p:Ekrem İmamoğlu]], the court in Silivri ordered a new expert report and adjourned to 12 Feb 2027. İmamoğlu said his company's car was lent to Beylikdüzü municipality free of charge and saved public money.
items.thread: Turkey fund crisis and opposition crackdown
items.notes: The indictment alleges a public loss of 122,305.70 lira and names 11 defendants. The Cumhuriyet link covers the first hearing on 22 Sept. The main İBB corruption trial continues separately.

items.text: Journalists' unions led by TGS held 'freedom for news' marches in 10 cities, the main one in Istanbul's Kadıköy, against arrests, court-appointed trustees at media outlets and website bans. Marchers read out the names of jailed journalists including Murat Ağırel, jailed on 19 Oct in a money-laundering probe, and BirGün's İsmail Arı, jailed on 21 Oct on a disinformation charge.
items.thread: Turkey fund crisis and opposition crackdown
items.notes: The date marks one year since a trustee was appointed at TELE1. Attendance: Cumhuriyet says 'hundreds', Sol Medya says 'thousands'. Ağırel was jailed in the probe into relatives of YENİ Parti MP Mustafa Sarıgül and denies the charges. Arı was jailed after a complaint by former RTÜK chair Ebubekir Şahin.

items.text: Erdoğan dismissed chief adviser Oktay Saral after Azerbaijan demanded it, amid a row over Baku's school headscarf restrictions. Baku had barred 31 Turkish nationals, including MPs Ömer Faruk Gergerlioğlu and [[p:Fatih Erbakan]], over their criticism.
items.outlet: Institute for Turkish Studies weekly bulletin
items.notes: Single bulletin summary; original Turkish press not yet checked. Other Turkish foreign-policy items that week: Canada–Turkey strategic partnership and free-trade talks (first round 30 Nov–4 Dec); eastern Libya's parliament ratified the 2019 Turkey maritime deal (20 Oct), and Greece and Egypt agreed to talks on extending their EEZ.
